text: Caldwell Ridge's prod network has a network security group protecting its first subnet, managed entirely by Terraform. Investigating a connectivity ticket on a Friday afternoon, a teammate opens the Azure Portal, finds nsg-cra-prod-web, and deletes it directly, convinced it's an orphaned leftover and forgetting it's Terraform-managed.

On Monday, terraform plan on envs/prod fails with a NetworkSecurityGroupNotFound error thrown against the subnet association, not plainly against the NSG itself. That's exactly why this kind of incident feels confusing -- nothing in the message says outright that someone deleted the NSG. It takes a careful read to connect the error back to a resource Terraform's state still insists exists.

Before running a single state-modifying command, pull a local backup: terraform state pull. The remote Azure Storage backend from Chapter 3 already keeps blob versions, but that's a safety net for the backend, not a substitute for a known-good local copy in hand right now. State surgery is unforgiving -- a wrong resource address can silently drop something Terraform still needs to track.

terraform state list confirms both the NSG and its association are still tracked, pointing at an object that no longer exists in Azure. From here there are two real situations, not one generic fix: either nothing has replaced the deleted NSG, or someone already recreated a lookalike by hand to unblock the same ticket.

If nothing replaced it, terraform state rm clears the stale entries -- editing only Terraform's bookkeeping, never touching Azure -- so the next plan shows a clean create instead of an error. If a teammate already rebuilt it by hand, terraform import adopts that real object into state instead of risking a duplicate, and an immediate terraform plan afterward surfaces exactly where its rules drifted from the code.

Caldwell Ridge's network survived a real, out-of-band deletion because the recovery followed a disciplined order: back up state, read it carefully, then choose state rm or import on purpose instead of guessing. Lesson 32 closes the chapter by tracing every one of this project's decisions back to the course chapter that made it possible.
